narrative.documentConcept: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API
narrative.text: Lighter is a ZK-rollup perp and spot DEX on Ethereum with a central limit order book. Standard accounts pay 0% maker and taker on regular perp and spot orders; the cost is a 300 ms delay on taker orders, cancels and modifies, and a 60 requests/minute API limit. Plus (0.005%, higher rate limits) and Premium/Advanced (0.004% maker, 0.028% taker, 140 ms, LIT-staking discounts, up to 72,000 sendTx/min) are opt-in via the changeAccountTier endpoint. Trading uses SignerClient-signed sendTx over REST or WebSocket with per-order nonces. Operational risk is real: the Oct 2025 single-sequencer outage, and the 16 Nov 2026 theft of about 10.39M USDC through keys recovered from nonce-reusing custom signing code. Critics call the zero fee a latency tax.

narrative.documentConcept: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API
narrative.text: Standard-account latency figures differ. The mainnet docs and the 2026-08-30 announcement give 300 ms taker, 300 ms cancel/modify and 0 ms post-only. A Medium review (Aug 2026) and the Robinhood Chain docs give 300 ms taker and 200 ms maker/cancel, and MarsBit and leviathan_news say 200-300 ms.

narrative.documentConcept: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API
narrative.text: Scope of the 40 requests per minute default transaction-type limit. The rate-limits table lists it as the Default for all account types, while the Premium/Plus sendTx buckets reach 4,000 to 72,000 per minute. NautilusTrader observed code 23000 after about 40 modifications in a minute, which suggests it can bind order transactions, but the account tier of that test is not stated.

narrative.documentConcept: Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API
narrative.text: Cause of the incident. Lighter's first update called it a leaked API key on one trader's account and pointed at one compromised outside party (per Bitquery). Its post-mortem is more specific: custom signing code reused signature nonces, so the keys were recoverable from public signatures.

narrative.documentConcept: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs
narrative.text: Perp DEXs other than Lighter and Paradex that advertise zero or near-zero fees: Aster, Extended, edgeX, GRVT, Pacifica and Variational Omni. Read closely, most are zero on the maker side only. Extended and Aster charge 2.5 and 4 bps taker, edgeX and Pacifica 4-4.5 bps at base tier, GRVT pays a tiny maker rebate and charges 4.5 bps taker, and only Variational charges no explicit fee (it prices via spread). API access is mature at Aster, Extended, edgeX and GRVT, but Variational's public API is read-only with trading API still unreleased as of mid-November. Zero-fee status is incentive-dependent and has been revised upward elsewhere.

narrative.documentConcept: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies
narrative.text: Alpha-signal market-making models (Cartea and Sanchez-Betancourt 2023, as described by Albers et al.) say predictive signals boost maker profitability, assuming a maker order fills when the next opposite taker arrives (front of queue). Albers et al. say that assumption is not generally tenable and find commonly-cited maker strategies highly unprofitable in live Binance BTC perpetual data.

narrative.documentConcept: Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies
narrative.text: The Daru Finance study finds the touch quoter's markout negative on crypto perpetuals but notes a companion CME study found half-spread and drift offsetting almost exactly; the two place the order at opposite ends of the queue, so the contrast cannot be attributed to asset class alone.

narrative.documentConcept: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs
narrative.text: ChainCatcher argues Lighter's 200-300 ms delay lets HFT market makers arbitrage retail, who may pay several times normal cost in implicit slippage; Castle Labs' measured cost to open a $100k BTC order on Lighter (0.41 bps) was lower than Hyperliquid (4.71 bps) and CEX medians.

narrative.documentConcept: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs
narrative.text: Which venue is cheapest depends on order size and on what is measured. OpenChainBench ranks Lighter first at a $1,000 notional and Castle Labs ranks it first at $100k BTC, both on cost that includes the taker fee. Castle Labs also finds Hyperliquid had the lowest median slippage at $1M, and OpenChainBench says deeper books can beat a zero fee at $1M.
